ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2026-01-15
Provider: Dr. Emily Zhang, MD
Department: Ophthalmology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Due to concerns about his vision.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for ophthalmologic follow-up in the setting of Neurofibromatosis type 1 and prior evaluations for visual concerns. They report that over the past few months, he has been bumping into objects on his right side and has difficulty seeing the board at school. His teacher also noticed that he tilts his head to the left when trying to focus on visual tasks.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Neurofibromatosis type 1 (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Acoustic neuroma (Vestibular schwannoma) (diagnosed 2025-01-15)
- Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder
- Visual impairment

His past medical history is significant for multiple café-au-lait spots noted since infancy, and a recent diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Methylphenidate 5 mg orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with neurofibromatosis type 1
- Maternal grandfather with unknown skin condition

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the child has six café-au-lait macules larger than 1.5 cm in diameter, axillary freckling, and two soft, pedunculated skin lesions on his back consistent with neurofibromas. Ophthalmologic examination reveals a right-sided proptosis and esotropia. Fundoscopic examination shows optic disc pallor on the right. There is no evidence of precocious puberty or bone abnormalities. His visual acuity is 20/200 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye.

Concerns about his skin and development

The patient returns to the Neurology clinic one year following his initial genetics evaluation for neurocutaneous findings. The parents report that their son has multiple brown spots on his skin that have been present since birth and seem to be increasing in number. They also mention that he has been struggling with learning at school.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:

- Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder
- Visual impairment

NKDA

There is no family history of similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY:

VITAL SIGNS:
His blood pressure is within normal limits.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Sharma, MD
Department: Neurology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Brought to the pediatrician by his parents due to concerns about his vision

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns to the neurology clinic for ongoing care, previously evaluated by genetics in 2020 and in this department in 2021. They report that he often bumps into objects and has difficulty seeing things on his left side. His academic performance has declined over the past year, and his teacher has noticed that he frequently squints and tilts his head when trying to read the board.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Neurofibromatosis type 1 (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder
- Visual impairment

His medical history is significant for multiple café-au-lait macules larger than 1.5 cm in diameter and axillary freckling.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Methylphenidate 5 mg orally twice daily

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with neurofibromatosis type 1
- Maternal grandfather with unknown skin condition

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, Lisch nodules are noted on slit-lamp examination. His visual acuity is decreased in the left eye. Fundoscopic examination reveals an optic disc with blurred margins on the left.

IMAGING:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain with contrast shows a mass lesion along the optic pathway.
